25dee9f382: Twenty-three figures of speech in five families

b7343fd806: Allusion, parody, pun, irony, two-part allegorical saying, inversion, alliteration and assonance
6ca573854b: Rhetoric brings words to life, but cram too many techniques into one line and listeners can't find the point.
ed725a7e6a: Uses interjections and particles to show surprise, sorrow, regret or hope.
3f71297d23: 怎麼了 你累了 說好的幸福呢<cite>Vincent Fang 〈說好的幸福呢〉</cite>
b54bbf31fe: Turns suddenly from statement to question to catch attention and make the other person reflect.
da531b9612: 你還記得嗎 記憶裡的炎夏<cite>Lee Cheuk-hung 〈愛〉</cite>
1c32b8a02f: Calls out and talks directly to someone who isn't there, strengthening first-person feeling.
cea7c44664: 分手快樂 祝你快樂 你可以找到更好的<cite>Yao Jo-lung 〈分手快樂〉</cite>
3f2021c06d: Uses one thing to describe another: the known to explain the unknown, the concrete to explain the abstract.
a32364aa5d: 愛情好像流沙 我不掙扎<cite>Wawa 〈流沙〉</cite>
9c1f4cc3b7: Changes a thing's nature: objects as people, people as objects, the abstract made concrete.
1328185f20: 愛情不停站 想開往地老天荒<cite>Lin Xi 〈愛情轉移〉</cite>
24de77b72d: Uses concrete images to express unseen ideas and feelings.
a7dfc5ae8c: 沒結果的花 未完成的牽掛<cite>Lee Cheuk-hung 〈愛〉</cite>
c60fc6e86e: Doesn't use the thing's real name, but something related in its place.
4c8e698045: 你最後一身紅 殘留在我眼中<cite>Shih Yi-lang 〈曲終人散〉</cite>
3eda20593d: Goes beyond the facts to deepen the impression; coming from real feeling, it won't be mistaken for fact.
8e3ea96587: 我的心已經飛到這個城市的另一邊<cite>Wawa 〈天天〉</cite>
9c345b9b36: Depicts the sounds, colours and states of things to make the picture three-dimensional.
cade09ff71: 天青色等煙雨 而我在等妳<cite>Vincent Fang 〈青花瓷〉</cite>
18c69b4fc3: Puts opposite ideas side by side; the stronger the contrast, the sharper the impression.
e94b199c20: 牽手的時候太冷清 擁抱的時候不夠靠近<cite>Yang Li-te 〈他不愛我〉</cite>
7be6203277: Two lines with the same number of characters and similar syntax, neat in form and harmonious in sound.
5327141d5c: 人變了心 言而無信 人斷了情 無謂傷心<cite>Lin Chiu-li 〈剪愛〉</cite>
859aa404aa: Three or more lines in a row presenting images of the same kind; they needn't be the same length.
ecb6abf4fa: 我不要你的承諾 不要你的永遠<cite>Wu Yu-kang 〈原來你什麼都不要〉</cite>
7e1f4f7fda: Repeats the same word in a row to show time and space stretching on.
b4ac0419e1: 我願意為你 我願意為你<cite>Yao Chien 〈我願意〉</cite>
c5c0403475: Arranges things layer by layer by depth, order or size.
a1cf455b60: 一步兩步三步四步望著天<cite>Jay Chou 〈星晴〉</cite>
b6aafe7348: The end of one line becomes the start of the next.
693e03e72f: 說再見 再見不會太遙遠<cite>Ding Hsiao-wen 〈祝福〉</cite>
37980eecaa: Mostly the same words, in exactly reversed order.
18c1ef0109: 孤單是一個人的狂歡 狂歡是一群人的孤單<cite>Chen Hsiao-chuan 〈葉子〉</cite>
91279ae04f: Borrows famous sayings, classical references or proverbs, using common ground to persuade.
cb653a5a1a: 寫下我 度秒如年難捱的離騷<cite>Qing Feng 〈小情歌〉</cite>
63aad161b0: Swaps words in a familiar phrase to say something new; common in song and album titles.
5356b25744: 陽光宅男, 無樂不作, 魔杰座<cite>Song and album titles</cite>
cde2848a51: Uses a word's multiple meanings or a sound-alike to give a line a double meaning.
059cd11d1e: 你說水星它沒有衛星好孤獨<cite>Lin Xi 〈想哭〉</cite>
16d9960cfe: Irony, two-part allegorical saying, inversion, alliteration and assonance
e095d8cae8: Says the opposite of what's meant to express what's meant; often used for satire.
d4759d7bb8: 這個家園充滿芬芳的青草<cite>Tom Chang 〈動物的悲歌〉</cite>
b7ece41700: The first half makes a comparison and the second half explains it; also called a hidden saying.
db104f75ff: 我乾杯你隨意<cite>Hsu Chang-te 〈婚禮的祝福〉</cite>
364583ed73: Deliberately reverses normal word order; common in work with a classical flavour.
2e02f2e4e7: 如傳世的青花瓷自顧自美麗<cite>Vincent Fang 〈青花瓷〉</cite>
b694b13fba: Uses words that share initials or finals to strengthen the rhythm.
7c9edca196: 嘆惜著誰又被傷了心 卻還不清醒<cite>Lin Chiu-li 〈聽海〉</cite>
8d676cabaf: As you listen, find at least two figures of speech
6b8c05d41d: 〈聽海〉: second-person rhetorical questions, alliteration and assonance. 〈天天〉: repetition and hyperbole. 〈婚禮的祝福〉: the palindrome 「我的請帖是你的喜帖」 and a two-part allegorical saying. 〈愛〉: rhetorical questions, transference and symbolism.
9fb0733e16: Which figure of speech does this line use?
fc70c9f04a: "Loneliness" leaves: an abstract feeling is given a human action, which is transference in the form of personification.
7896af7e4e: The first clause ends on 「給」 and the next begins with 「能給」: anadiplosis.
7c909227a4: 「太多太多」 repeats back to back, which is repetition; the contrast between the two lines also has the effect of contrast.
21ca812b54: Turning from statement to question to catch the listener's attention: a rhetorical question.
